cards.text: Friend, the writer of Hebrews has been telling his readers about a new covenant God promised. Now he looks back at the first covenant. It had rules for worship, plus a sanctuary right here on earth.

A tabernacle was set up, and its first room held the lampstand, the table and the consecrated bread. After all those years in one junk drawer, friend, I get EXCITED about anything with more than one room.

cards.question: That first room, with the lampstand, the table and the consecrated bread, had a name. What was it called?

cards.text: Behind the second curtain is another room, the Most Holy Place. It has the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant.

cards.question: Inside the ark of the covenant are the gold jar of manna and the stone tablets of the covenant. What else is in there?

cards.text: Above the ark are the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. Friend, that is a WHOLE lot of gold for one little room.

cards.question: Next, the writer of Hebrews walks through the cherubim and the mercy seat in full detail.

cards.text: He says we can't get into these things in detail right now. Friend, I respect that kind of self-control, because I can't describe ONE sprinkle in under ten minutes.
With everything set up, the priests go into that first room regularly to do their sacred duties.

cards.question: The priests go into the first room regularly. Who goes into the second room, the Most Holy Place?
The high priest goes into the Most Holy Place only ___ a year.
Every time the high priest goes into the Most Holy Place, he never goes in without ___.
The high priest offers that blood for the sins the people committed in ignorance, and also for ___.

cards.text: Now the writer says the Holy Spirit was showing something through this whole arrangement.

cards.question: As long as the first tabernacle was still standing, the way into the Most Holy Place was wide open.

cards.text: The writer calls it an illustration for the present time. And the gifts and sacrifices offered there had a limit.

cards.question: The gifts and sacrifices offered in the tabernacle had a limit. What couldn't they do for the worshiper?

cards.text: Those gifts and sacrifices deal only with food and drink and special washings, outside rules. That's like me shining my gold base till it SPARKLES while my insides are still packed with drawer dust.

cards.question: Those rules about food and drink and special washings were meant to stay in place forever.

cards.text: Friend, put the dough DOWN, because here comes the turn. Christ comes as high priest of the good things that have come.

cards.question: Christ, the high priest, goes through a tabernacle too. Which one?

answers.text: A greater one not made by hands

cards.text: And Christ doesn't go in by the blood of goats and calves. Lean in for this one, friend.

cards.question: Christ doesn't use the blood of goats and calves. So how does He enter the Most Holy Place?
Like the high priest, Christ has to go back into the Most Holy Place every year.

cards.text: Once for all. ONE time, friend. Meanwhile it takes me three tries to get a single batch to come out right.

cards.question: By entering once for all with His own blood, Christ secured redemption that is ___.

cards.text: Now the writer reasons it out. If the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkled on people who are ceremonially unclean, make their bodies clean…

cards.question: If the old blood could make bodies clean, how much more will the blood of Christ do what?

answers.text: Purify our consciences from works of death
Keep our bodies clean for longer
Make the old tabernacle holy again

cards.text: Christ, through the eternal Spirit, offered Himself unblemished to God. Friend, He brought HIMSELF.

cards.question: Christ's blood purifies our consciences so that we may serve the living God.

cards.text: From works of death to serving the living God. I went from the back of a junk drawer to my own bakery, friend, and I STILL can't top that trade.

findings.problem: The opening card states a fact from outside the passage: the writer has been telling his readers about a new covenant God promised (Hebrews 8:8-13). The card gives no reference for it and cites only Hebrews 9:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Nothing on card 6 sets up this true or false question about whether the writer will discuss the cherubim and mercy seat in detail. The baker can only guess. The question also asks about an aside that doesn't move the passage forward, and card 8 then simply tells the answer.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin's insides are still packed with drawer dust. This adds something new to his backstory and contradicts it, because he was renewed when he left the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Christ appears for the first time in the walkthrough, and the card doesn't say simply who He is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. "A greater one not made by hands" is the only description. The two wrong answers are named, man-made buildings, so the phrase "not made by hands" points straight to the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The last card repeats "from works of death" and "serve the living God," which cards 9 and 11 already covered. It doesn't move the passage forward.

The punchline "I STILL can't top that trade" is unclear. It isn't obvious whose trade can't be topped, or how his move from the drawer to the bakery compares with Christ purifying consciences. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
